newsitem.title: USA: Outboard says July announcement likely.
newsitem.headline: Outboard says July announcement likely.

text.p: Outboard Marine Corp said Wednesday it likely will make an announcement this month on strategic alternatives that it said in late April it was examining with the help of Salomon Brothers.
"We probably should be announcing something this month," said Outboard director of strategic planning Stan Main in an interview with Reuters. He declined to provide more details.
Outboard has no reason to deviate from the 60- to 90-day timetable it outlined April 25, when it said it had hired Salomon to look into alternatives, Main said.
At that time, Waukegan, Ill.-based Outboard said those alternatives could include a sale of the company, merger, joint venture or an equity offer.
Heavy trading in Outboard options Wednesday on the Chicago Board Options Exchange indicated the market expects the company will announce soon that it is being acquired.
"They're looking for something to come out in the next two weeks or so," said Tom Coogan, a CBOE trader, who noted heavy out-of-the-money Outboard call buying.
On the New York Stock Exchange, shares in the maker of outboard boats and boat engines hit a new 12-month high of 18-13/16, up 1-1/8, on moderate volume early Wednesday.
The shares have moved up strongly from the low teens on strong expectations of a deal since late April, said Wall Street analysts.
Outboard announced June 17 that it had signed a long-term deal with Suzuki Motor Corp in which Outboard will buy selected outboard engines from the Japanese manufacturer.
Outboard has had a stern-drive manufacturing joint venture with AB Volvo since 1993.

Outboard is the largest U.S. maker of outboard engines and the second-largest builder of recreational powerboats. Its brands include Evinrude and Johnson motors, as well as Chris-Craft, Four Winns, Grumman, Stratos and Javelin.
